name: Iram
overview: Iram was a male Edomite who held the position of chief of Edom, as recorded in Genesis 36:43. His leadership role identifies him as a significant figure within the Edomite tribe. There are no additional notes or details about his life beyond his tribal affiliation and leadership.
namesAndTitles: The name Iram appears as a proper name in Genesis 36:43. There is no specific meaning or divine origin attributed to his name in the biblical text, so it is simply recognized as his personal name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Iram was a descendant of Esau, linking him to the Edomite lineage. No other family relationships are recorded for Iram beyond this connection to Esau.
scriptureSignificance: Iram's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as a chief of Edom, demonstrating the established leadership structure among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:43 underscores the organization and governance within the Edomite people, highlighting the continuation of Esau's lineage through notable leaders like Iram.
